candidate.blueprint_locator: Printed p.12, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — prepare and administer medications safely and review medication-specific administration requirements
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — enteral-tube medication administration
candidate.educational_objective: Administer enteral-tube medications one at a time and flush between medications, while accounting for formulation suitability, fluid status, and agency policy.

options.A: Mix all medications into the enteral formula before administration.
options.B: Combine all medications in one syringe and give them together without flushing between drugs.
options.C: Administer each medication separately and flush the tube between medications according to the client's fluid status and agency policy.
options.D: Crush every solid medication together because formulation type does not affect tube administration.

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills guidance instructs nurses to prepare and administer enteral-tube medications individually rather than mixing them because mixing can cause incompatibilities, altered drug response, or tube obstruction. The tube is flushed between medications, with the amount adjusted when clinically indicated such as fluid restriction and according to agency policy. C is therefore correct. A, B, and D conflict with safe medication-preparation and administration principles.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Multiple enteral-tube medications should be prepared/administered separately and the tube flushed between medications; formulation suitability and fluid restrictions must be considered.
